question.problem:
$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{3(x+y)}{4}, & 0<x\le 2y,\,\,0<y\le 1, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}\,{f}_{Y}(y)=\{\begin{aligned}3{y}^{2}, & 0<y\le 1, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Let $X$ and $Y$  be continuous random variables. Their joint probability density function and the marginal probability density function of $Y$ are shown above. Find the conditional variance $\text{Var}[X\,|\,Y=1]$ given that the corresponding expected value is ${\mu }_{X|1}=\frac{7}{6}.$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that the conditional variance of $X$ given $Y=y$ is defined by

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X\,|\,Y=y] & =\text{E}[(X-{\mu }_{X|y})^{2}\,|\,Y=y] \\  & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}\,|\,Y=y]-{\mu }_{X|y}^{2},\end{aligned}
$$

where 

$$
\text{E}[{X}^{2}\,|\,Y=y]={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }{x}^{2}\,{f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,y)\,\text{d}x.
$$

Note that $\text{E}[X\,|\,Y=y]$ is a function of $y.$ 

The conditional density function of $X$ given $Y=y$ can be computed as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,y) & =\frac{f(x,y)}{{f}_{Y}(y)} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{3(x+y)}{4})}{3{y}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{x+y}{4{y}^{2}},\end{aligned}
$$

where $0<x\le 2y,\,0<y\le 1.$ Outside this domain, we have ${f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,y)=0.$ 

Now, substituting $y=1$ into the expression for ${f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,y),$ we get

$$
{f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,1)=\frac{x+1}{4}.
$$

 

Therefore, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}\,|\,Y=1]{\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }{x}^{2}\,{f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,1)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{x}^{2}\cdot \frac{(x+1)}{4}\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{4}{\int }_{0}^{2}({x}^{3}+{x}^{2})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{4}{[\frac{{x}^{4}}{4}+\frac{{x}^{3}}{3}]}_{0}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}(4+\frac{8}{3})-0 \\  & =\frac{1}{4}(\frac{20}{3}) \\  & =\frac{5}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X\,|\,Y=1] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}\,|\,Y=1]-{\mu }_{X|1}^{2} \\  & =\frac{5}{3}-{(\frac{7}{6})}^{2} \\  & =\frac{5}{3}-\frac{49}{36} \\  & =\frac{11}{36}.\end{aligned}
$$
